page: Microsoft Azure M32bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz, featuring 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture.

This server does not include local storage, relying instead on external block storage with Premium Storage capabilities. It contains no GPU accelerators. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8), which accelerate vector and matrix operations.

Performance benchmarks show strong capabilities in single-core and multi-core operations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2210.0 and a multi-core score of 18347.0. It demonstrates top-tier performance in small-model LLM text generation and strong throughput in static web serving at 53.69 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks drops to 182.67 GB/sec for reads and 86.71 GB/sec for writes. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation scoring in the bottom 25% at 2.74 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M32bs_v3 offers a dense memory profile and high-frequency dedicated compute resources suitable for memory-intensive enterprise applications without the overhead of local NVMe drives. It is well-suited for workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, medium-scale data processing, web serving, and software compilation.
